drafts.title: There is no "Veterans & Retired Seniors Grant." AI fakes are stealing VA checks (AP6, AI and scams for normal people / 55+ and veterans)
drafts.window: Tue 11 AM-12 PM MT (very strong Tuesday cell). Don't run it the same day as AP8 (trip AI question).
drafts.angle: veterans and retirees are a big slice of his 55+ audience. VA just warned about a fake Facebook grant ad, made to look government-sponsored, that got vets to hand over direct-deposit info. Pair with the FBI's Oct 15 AI-impersonation alert. Pure safety, nonpartisan, and the honest side of "AI for the masses": the tool isn't scary, the crooks using it are.
bullets: VA News (updated Oct 13, 2026): a fake "Veterans & Retired Seniors Grant Program" post on Facebook looked sponsored by a government official; some veterans gave direct-deposit info, had benefits redirected, and lost thousands. VA says it's working to make them whole.
VA warning signs: "act now," keep it secret, a voice or video that seems a little off, asks for private info. Rule: stop, check, then act. VA fraud line: 833-38V-SAFE (833-388-7233).
FBI IC3 alert Oct 15, 2026: scammers use AI to make realistic voices, images and texts impersonating government agencies and trusted contacts. Report at ic3.gov.
National Elder Fraud Hotline: 1-833-372-8311.
Pixel: 20 sec talk-to-camera: "If an ad says there's a grant for veterans and wants your bank info, it's fake. Call VA yourself."
Premium reply/quote: AARP Fraud Watch Network or a large veterans-service account posting about scams this week. One line with the VA number and "call back on a number you look up."
drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:
There is no "Veterans & Retired Seniors Grant."

VA says a fake Facebook ad, made to look official, got vets to hand over direct-deposit info. Their benefit checks went to crooks.

If it says "act now," stop and call VA yourself: 833-388-7233.

[my take: ___]

Know a vet who should see this?

LONGER VERSION:
Heads up for every veteran and every family with one.

VA says scammers ran a fake Facebook ad for a "Veterans & Retired Seniors Grant Program." It looked like a government official was behind it. People handed over their direct-deposit info, and their VA payments got rerouted. Some lost thousands.

The FBI put out a warning Oct 15 that crooks are using AI to fake voices, photos and texts that look like they come from the government or someone you trust.

Our house rule:
1. Nobody changes a bank deposit from an ad, a text or a call.
2. Hang up and call back on a number you look up yourself.
3. Ask a family member before you act.

VA fraud line: 833-388-7233. Elder Fraud Hotline: 1-833-372-8311.
